searches.note: Twenty one searches of twenty eight, seven unspent. Six were restricted to a house's own domain (d'Arenberg twice, Wirra Wirra, Hardys, Kay Brothers, Yangarra); others blocked the author's main sources. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record read with one instruction, refute it: dates, people, grapes, sites, making, ageing, serving, label, story, cards and questions, then the house rules.
Edits made in place; the fragment lints sound with five records refuted.

tested: Founding 1912, the racehorses sold, Joseph Osborn dead in 1921 aged 67, the son Frank given up medicine through ill health: the house's timeline (searched on its domain) and two secondary accounts. Sound, save the son's first vintage in 1912, refuted.
The winery built in the late 1920s (1927 or 1928 by account) and the first vintage of 1928: two secondary accounts and the house's tour page. Added as the late 1920s.
Helena d'Arenberg dead soon after d'Arry's birth, the red stripe of 1959, d'Arry's charge from 1957, aged 95 at death: The Shout and two accounts. Sound.
The Dead Arm: released 1993 by the house's Dead Arm Distinction page and two merchants. The early 1990s kept.

Making from the house's sheets of 2004 to 2019: open fermenters, foot treading two thirds through, basket press, barrel finish, lees unracked, no fining or filtration, 18 to 21 months. Sound, details added.
The Cube opened on 14 December 2017: Good Design, Concrete Playground, Gourmet on the Road. Sound.

changes.why: the first vintage was of 1928 and the founder's illness is in no source; teetotal in one account only

swaps.why: The author proposed no swap; the five picks stand as the plan has them.

rules: No living person named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash: read across all five records after the edits. The notes on highest in Yangarra stand on the house's sheets and a merchant (the highest section of the 1946 planting).
codexTension: The library record p-darenberg names Chester Osborn, a living person, in its holdings line, and ranks d'Arenberg the house most often named for McLaren Vale; reported, not edited.
The region record calls High Sands the reference for the modern style, a ranking; reported, not edited.
